chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

You should say three times, when you look at the afflicted one, without him hearing it: 'The Praise is for Allah Who gave me well-being from what He afflicted you with, and had He willed, He would have done so.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says that will not be struck by that affliction ever.'

key_terms.لَوْ شَاءَ فَعَلَ: Had He willed, He would have done so

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to say when seeing someone who is suffering or afflicted?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific dhikr for observing affliction, highlighting the Shia emphasis on 'shukr al-ni'mah' (gratitude for blessings) as a means of preservation from future trials. The promise of protection underscores the theological principle that mindful gratitude acts as a spiritual shield, reinforcing the ethical duty to acknowledge divine decree without ostentation.
